title: Enterprise request: economic-slice and technical touchpoint mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a repeatable rapid-scan template that turns a batch of Sales/CS enterprise feature asks into: (1) an economic slice (rough monthly cost / potential revenue or retention impact), (2) a technical touchpoint map (what Redwood components must change: API, runtime, Dedicated, Private, Console), and (3) an initial risk & compliance checklist. Scope: non-bug feature requests routed from Sales/CS. Excludes deep product redesigns and multi-quarter platform projects; those will be flagged for a follow-on PRD. Deliverables: 1) a compact Confluence template for intake analysis, 2) a triage rubric and scoring sheet, 3) a two-slide exec summary template for Sales handoff, 4) sample outputs for three real customer asks. Acceptance criteria: - Template converts a list of 10 requests into ranked priorities within 2 hours. - Each prioritized request includes a numeric economic slice, a mapped list of technical touchpoints, and a compliance flag. - Hand-off slide generated for Sales contains estimated implementation tiers (Quick: <4w, Medium: 4-12w, Large: >12w). - Security/compliance-required flags include suggested owners and next steps. Success metrics: time-to-first-scope, agreement rate with Eng/Design on tiering (>80% in review), and Sales satisfaction score (target >=4/5).
comments: 2026-02-25 - Kickoff: scoped with Sales ops (Lina Choudhury) and Solutions Eng (Ravi Mehta). Agreed to focus on asks where customer explicitly requests Dedicated or Private deployment paths.

2026-03-01 - First draft of rubric reviewed by Eng leads (Eva Liu). Trade-off called out: economic slices rely on rough usage assumptions; decided to capture assumptions explicitly per request instead of forcing a single model.
2026-03-04 - Design review: requested a compact two-slide handoff rather than a longer doc. UX asked for a one-line 'implementation driver' label (e.g., latency, isolation, compliance, custom-model).

2026-03-08 - Engineering comment (Miguel): added touchpoint mapping for Dedicated capacity (autoscaling policy, reserved pool sizing) and Private (VPC, KMS). Noted dependency on runtime-1.21 planned kernels work for quantized models.
2026-03-10 - PM review: prioritized 3 pilot accounts for sample outputs; identified one ask requiring security_review_required. Raised to Security team; SSO/KMS hit expected.
2026-03-12 - Current blocker: we need an estimate cadence from Infra for on-prem installation timelines. Follow-up action assigned to infra PM (ENG-21345).
acceptance_criteria: Batch of 10 Sales/CS asks processed and ranked with economic slice and tech map within 2 hours
Each output has explicit assumptions for traffic, token mix, and sequence length distribution
Tech touchpoints enumerate impacted layers (API, runtime, Dedicated autoscale, Private infra, Console flows)
Security/compliance flag present with next-step owner assigned for flagged items
Sample slides delivered for 3 pilot accounts and validated with Sales and Solutions Eng
notes: Implementation patterns observed: (A) UX/Console-only changes (low cost), (B) Runtime config/quantization/profile changes (medium), (C) Dedicated/private infra + compliance (high)
Trade-offs: accuracy of economic slices vs speed. We favor speed for first-pass; include confidence bucket (low/med/high) to indicate estimation stability.

Decision log: use tiering thresholds Quick/Medium/Large to align with Eng planning. Quick = <4w dev + config; Medium = 4-12w dev or infra changes; Large = >12w or requires dedicated infra purchase or cross-team program.
Follow-ups: get an on-prem install SOW template from Infra, finalize the pricing assumptions sheet with Finance, schedule a 60-minute pilot run with Sales ops and Solutions Eng on 2026-03-18.
